name: card
description: A bounded thing in a list of things. Twelve near-identical spellings on the site — `rounded-xl border border-border/25 bg-surface-raised px-4 py-4`, then `px-5 py-5`, `px-5 py-7`, `p-5 sm:p-6`, `p-6` — seven different paddings for one idea, each one chosen by eye at a call site. Distinct from `surface`, which is any padded box; a card is a card because something can be DONE with it, so it has a hover and a selected state and `surface` does not.

base.transition: border-color var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), transform var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out)

featured.$description: One card in a set, lifted. A grid where every card is featured is a grid where none is — this exists so the eye has somewhere to land, which four equal cards never give it.

quiet.$description: Not yet real — a skill that is coming, a slot not filled. A dashed edge says `placeholder` in a way a fainter fill does not.

hover.$description: A lift, and the border warms. Not a background change — a card that fills on hover fights every badge and chip inside it.

reducedMotion.$description: The lift goes; the border still warms, so hover is still legible.

a11y.note: When the whole card is a link, it is ONE `<a>` wrapping the content — not a div with an onclick and a link inside it, which gives a keyboard user two targets for one destination and a screen reader a link whose name is the entire card. Anything genuinely separate inside (a menu, a secondary action) has to sit outside that link.
